coaching_implication: Coach the rep to answer 'who are you calling from' with full specificity every time — company name plus the form reference plus reassurance — rather than a one-word company name, since this is the exact moment the how_did_you_get_my_number protocol exists for.

quote: So are you able to access the power bill online, like, through Excel?
stewart_read: The customer had just given a bill figure ('$1.80 a month' — almost certainly a garbled transcription of a real number) and the rep does not acknowledge or reflect the figure at all, jumping straight to asking about online access.
alternative_hypothesis: The transcription of the bill figure is visibly corrupted ('$1.80 a month' is an implausible utility bill amount), so the rep may have heard a real, sensible number that simply didn't transcribe cleanly — in which case the rep's silent move to the next verify step is still a missed anchor, but the miss may be a transcription artifact rather than a rep failure to register the number.
coaching_implication: Regardless of the exact figure, the rep should be coached to always verbally reflect the bill amount back to the customer ('so around $180 a month, got it') — this both confirms the number for the record and creates the forward-pulling hook the schema calls for.

stewart_read: No day or time is set; the appointment is entirely contingent on the customer sending a bill photo at some future point, with 'then I can schedule you' left open-ended.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer is traveling and cannot access his bill for several days, a hard-locked appointment time may genuinely not be feasible on this call — the rep's deferred plan could be the practical, strategic move rather than a procedural miss.
coaching_implication: Even when a firm time can't be locked, the rep should still anchor a specific callback day/time rather than leaving it fully open — the customer explicitly offered a preferred window afterward, and the rep should have looped back to confirm it as a scheduled callback rather than letting the call end on 'take care.'
